title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a notion of 'atelier' (workshop). An atelier is a set 𝔉 of 'figures' with an order ≤ and a second relation ≪, subject to axioms At 1–At 7. Inside 𝔉 sits the set M of 'figures élémentaires', the (strictly) irreducible figures. For F ∈ 𝔉 he writes F̃ = {X ∈ M | X ≤ F} = {X | X ◁ F}. This belongs to his programme of an axiomatic, combinatorial 'tame topology'. The previous page defined a closed part 𝔉' ⊂ 𝔉 to be 'spacieuse' if it is stable under arbitrary sups. It also worked the example 𝔉 = 𝔓(I). There, closed parts made of finite sets are simplicial complexes on I, while spacious ones are just 𝔓(I') for a subset I' ⊂ I.

This page states a Proposition. Grothendieck notes it does not really depend on the axioms, only on the relations between ≤ and ≪ on 𝔉. It gives mutually inverse bijections
 Sousatspac(𝔉) ⇄ Ferm(M),
 𝔉' ↦ 𝔉' ∩ M,
 M' ↦ Env(M') := {F ∈ 𝔉 | F̃ ⊂ M'}.
On the left are spacious closed parts (spacious sub-ateliers) of 𝔉; on the right are 'closed' subsets of the elementary figures. The word 'fermées' on the M side is struck through in the body text, but 'Ferm(M)' remains in the displayed formula.

Modern reading. M is join-dense in 𝔉 (this is At 2: F = sup F̃). A sup-closed down-set of 𝔉 is then determined by its trace on M. Conversely, a subset M' ⊂ M generates the down-set of elements whose elementary pieces all lie in M'. For this to be stable under sups, M' must be closed for the closure 'X ∈ cl(S) iff X ≤ sup S'. That is the classical correspondence between a join-dense subset and the closure system it induces.

He then starts checking that a closed part 𝔉', with the induced ≤ and ≪, again satisfies At 1–At 7. He recalls the first three axioms:
- At 1: sups (bounded or nonempty families, for ≤) exist in 𝔉, and 𝔉 ≠ ∅, so 𝔉 has a least element ∅_𝔉.
- At 2: every F is the sup, for ≤, of the elementary (strictly irreducible) figures it majorizes.
- At 3: for F, G ∈ 𝔉, the join F ∨ G exists (i.e. {F, G} is majorized) as soon as X ∨ Y exists for all X ◁ F, Y ◁ G.

The next page shows At 1 and At 2 pass to 𝔉' automatically. At 3 needs an extra condition (Sousat 2), which leads to the definition of sous-atelier.
errors: The bijection Sousatspac(𝔉) ↔ Ferm(M) holds only if 'fermé' in M means closed for the closure X ∈ cl(S) ⇔ X ≤ sup S (or the elementary figures are completely join-prime, as in 𝔓(I)). For an arbitrary subset M' ⊂ M, Env(M') need not be stable under sups, and Env(M') ∩ M can be strictly larger than M'. The page leaves this ambiguous: 'fermées' is struck out in the text but 'Ferm(M)' survives in the display.
Minor: the struck-out first lines define the inverse map before the notion of closedness on M is fixed. The proof is not written out; it is presumably considered evident.

ideas.what: Bijection between sup-stable closed (down-closed) parts of 𝔉 and closed subsets of the join-dense set M of elementary figures, via 𝔉' ↦ 𝔉' ∩ M and M' ↦ Env(M')
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between sup-closed down-sets of a lattice and closed sets of the closure system induced on a join-dense subset (Birkhoff / Dedekind–MacNeille type representation)

ideas.what: Axioms At 1–At 3 of an 'atelier': existence of sups, every figure is the sup of the elementary figures below it, existence of binary joins tested on elementary pieces
ideas.modern_name: Atomistic / join-generated (partial) lattice axioms; close to coherence conditions for a poset of polyhedra
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct standard credit; Grothendieck's own 'ateliers' framework for tame topology
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 'atelier' axiomatics appear only in these archive notes as far as known

ideas.what: Spacious sub-ateliers as the analogue of full sub-vertex-sets (𝔓(I')) as opposed to simplicial complexes (general closed parts)

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished axiomatic framework ('ateliers', with relations ≤, ≪ and axioms At 1–At 7) intended as a foundation for tame topology / analysis situs. Its development into a sub-object theory (sous-ateliers, spacious sub-ateliers) was not taken up in the literature. The page itself only proves an elementary lattice-theoretic bijection.
missed.quote: On a deux applications bijectives inverses l'une de l'autre ... Sousatspac(𝔉) ⟶ Ferm(M)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, and for comparison with o-minimality and with poset/lattice approaches to polyhedra. Mathematically this specific statement is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The Proposition is a standard join-dense / closure-system correspondence. The only notable content is the glimpse of the unpublished 'atelier' axiomatics, already a known feature of these archives.
transcription_corrections: 'At 2 Toute F ∈ 𝔉 a bonne sup.' should read 'Toute F ∈ 𝔉 est borne sup. pour ≤ des "figures élémentaires" (de plus strictement irr.) qu'elle majore'; i.e. 'irr.' (irréductibles), not 'inv.'.
'Sousatspac' abbreviates 'sous-ateliers spacieux'; the struck 'Satsp' is an earlier abbreviation of the same.
The left-margin struck note reads approximately: 'Je fais ici identifié 𝔉 à une partie de P(M), Env(M') = {F ∈ 𝔉 | F̃ ⊂ M'}'.

'Il faut voir, pour 𝔉 un atelier, si 𝔉' est un sous-atelier de 𝔉 pour ≤, ≪, au sens des axiomes At 1–At 7. Rappelons que ces axiomes ...' is a likely reading; 'non-joints' in At 1 is uncertain (possibly 'les sup. majorés' or 'non vides').
'Ferm(M)' (not 'Ferm (M)' as a different word) is the right side of the bijection.
